A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AnthroTAP despite the changed title and layout. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original tracker fine-tuning results on TAP-Vid and RoboTAP, comparisons with self-training, ablations, and analyses of generated trajectories.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds experiments comparing synthetic-human training, trajectory subsets, training-data quantities, and visibility prediction.

M1.justification: The SMPL/TokenHMR projection, ray-casting visibility, optical-flow consistency checks, normalized motion comparison, and trajectory rejection rules remain unchanged. Moving filtering details to Appendix C and explicitly stating that existing tracker losses are used do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: v2 adds training with BlinkVision synthetic human tracks in Table 5, extending the represented training data beyond the previously tested sources. Let’s Dance/Anthro-LD, Kubric, and the existing evaluation datasets remain; reduced-size and trajectory-selected subsets do not introduce new task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 5 adds LocoTrack trained with BlinkVision as a synthetic-data comparator to AnthroTAP training. The main benchmark comparator set in Table 1 and the CoTracker3 self-training comparison in Table 3 are retained.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce 250/500-video subsets, below-median angular-acceleration training, a low-diversity condition, visibility removal, and synthetic-human training. The original metrics, First/Strided protocols, resolution groups, and main training settings remain. Table 5 labels pretraining as Kub64, unlike Table 1’s Kub; this does not establish that the original experiments were changed.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands tests of the pipeline’s rationale: real pseudo-labels versus synthetic perfect labels (Table 5), trajectory complexity/diversity (Table 6), training-data scale (Table 10), and visibility prediction (Table 11). Existing human/non-human, self-training, filtering, clip-length, and dilation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The retained trajectory standard-deviation calculation defines a diversity metric, not experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: Previously reported benchmark and ablation values remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantive findings. BlinkVision training gives DAVIS AJ 64.2 versus 64.8 for AnthroTAP in Table 5. Low-complexity/low-diversity training gives AJ 66.0/66.6 versus 69.0 for the full dataset in Table 6. Table 10 reports AJ 65.6/65.7 with 250/500 videos; Table 11 reports 64.6 without visibility versus 65.9 for the full pipeline. These are added conditions, not improved versions of earlier scores.

T1.justification: The visibility rule, filtering mathematics, and trajectory complexity/diversity definitions are retained. The removed displayed visibility equation remains expressed in prose, and the new flow symbols are equivalent shorthand. No substantive mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that human-motion pseudo-labels enable strong general point tracking with substantially less real training data and computation. v2 foregrounds knowledge distillation and general-object transfer, but these reframe the existing contribution rather than materially changing its scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new experiments as supporting real-world visual characteristics despite imperfect labels, the usefulness of complex/diverse trajectories and visibility, and effective learning from small video subsets. Existing limitations concerning rejected useful tracks, inaccurate occlusion labels, and suitability as a benchmark remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page address and explicitly identifies reuse of each tracker’s original loss. However, it removes v1’s numerical filtering settings: delta_cons=1.0, tau_dist=1.0, epsilon_norm=2.0, epsilon_ratio=10^-6, and tau_ratio=0.25. Most optimizer, hardware, and training-budget details remain; code and dataset release is still described prospectively.

R1.justification: v2 adds the BlinkVision citation and comparison and removes the TAPIP3D citation. The main positioning against synthetic-only training and real-video self-training remains. L4P’s updated title and publication information refer to the same work.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the title and abstract, revises the introductory framing, consolidates the supervised-training exposition, and moves the detailed filtering subsection into Appendix C. Trajectory metrics receive a main-text summary, the DriveTrack comparison moves into the main analysis, and the appendices are reorganized.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the single-column format with a two-column layout, reformats tables and captions, and adds four analysis tables. All eight illustrations retain their content, but several are resized or relocated: the filtering diagram moves to the appendix, while the DriveTrack comparison moves into the main text.

improvement.justification: The new comparisons and ablations in Tables 5, 6, 10, and 11 provide useful evidence about training-data characteristics, data efficiency, and visibility that v1 lacked. This strengthens the empirical rationale without changing the main benchmark results. The gain is limited by incomplete documentation of the new controls, including low-diversity selection, and the removal of numerical filtering hyperparameters that v1 supplied.
